title: Canonical map from the generation locus of a line module into relative Proj
statement: Let $S,T$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and $f:X\to T$ a morphism over $S$. Let $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}\mathcal A_d$ be a quasi-coherent graded $\mathcal O_T$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra] [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures], let $L$ be a line module on $X$, and let $\psi:f^*\mathcal A\to\bigoplus_{d\geq0}L^{\otimes d}$ be a graded algebra homomorphism on the small etale site, with tensor pullback $f^*$ along the induced ringed-topos map. Let $U(\psi)\subseteq X$ be the union over $d\geq1$ of the loci where $\psi_d:f^*\mathcal A_d\to L^{\otimes d}$ is surjective. This is an open subspace, and there is a canonical $T$-morphism $r_{L,\psi}:U(\psi)\to\operatorname{Proj}_T(\mathcal A)$ [def-nagata-relative-proj]. For any commutative diagram of $S$-spaces\n$$\begin{array}{ccc} X' &\xrightarrow{g'}& X\\ f'\downarrow &&\downarrow f\\ T'&\xrightarrow{g}&T,\end{array}$$\nwhere $X'$ and $T'$ are schemes and $g,g'$ are arbitrary morphisms, put $\mathcal A'=g^*\mathcal A$, let $L'=(g')^*L$, and let $\psi'$ be the pulled-back graded homomorphism. Then $U(\psi')=(g')^{-1}(U(\psi))$, and under the canonical isomorphism $\operatorname{Proj}_{T'}(\mathcal A')\simeq T'\times_T\operatorname{Proj}_T(\mathcal A)$ the map $r_{L',\psi'}$ is the base change of $r_{L,\psi}$. On schemes this is the usual canonical morphism obtained from the graded maps into tensor powers of an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module], with pullback [def-pc-module-pullback].

proof.text: For each section of this subfunctor on W, apply [lem-trf-space-line-test-map] to the associated generating scheme test. Precomposition preserves IsCanonicalTestMap by associativity and the test-to-base equation. Test-map uniqueness therefore makes these morphisms natural, defining r. Applying the formula to the identity test gives IsCanonicalMap. Conversely naturality transports the IsCanonicalMap formula to all further tests, so test-map uniqueness gives sectionwise uniqueness of r.

proof.text: For a base-change square, [lem-trf-space-line-test-base-change] identifies generation sets on every scheme test. Yoneda naturality identifies the composite test with that of the image section, proving IsGenerationOpen for the inverse-image subfunctor. The pulled-back family is coherent by the original identity and composition equations. Apply the preceding natural-transformation construction to obtain r′. Naturality transports the canonical-map predicate to canonical-test predicates; the test base-change comparison gives the required equality sectionwise. The same uniqueness proves the displayed unique existence of r′ and r. The identity-test formula is exactly the usual scheme construction.
